text:
maya: Heads-up — customer 'acme' says their Grafana dashboards show no series for `app_requests`. I opened their dashboard and Explore returns 0 series. Anyone know where to start looking for the Prometheus remote_write endpoint for their VPC? cc @priya

priya: For Private/VPC customers we tag traffic with X-Scope-OrgID. Their tenant id should be `acme-42`. Grafana datasource points at our proxy: https://prom-remote-write.redwood-inference/api/v1/receive (tenant path handled by header). In Grafana Explore try: `sum(rate(app_requests[5m])) by (status)`. If you get 0 series, first check prom-remote-write auth and network egress.

maya: I tried Explore and it shows 0 series but no obvious error in UI. The customer said their promtail logs look normal. They also mentioned TLS errors when trying to curl our receiver from a pod.

devon: Typical triage I run (short):
1) `kubectl -n observability logs promtail-xxxx` -> look for remote_write errors (queue, auth).
2) Check proxy/collector logs on our side: `kubectl -n infra logs prom-remote-proxy-xxx` or host path `/var/log/otel/collector.log`.
3) From a customer pod run a simple curl to validate connectivity/headers: `curl -v -H "X-Scope-OrgID: acme-42" https://prom-remote-write.redwood-inference/api/v1/receive/status`

priya: Also ask them to run an ephemeral pod that has curl (some clusters block egress via HTTP proxy). Example debug command I usually give them:
`kubectl run -i --rm debug --image=alpine -- sh -c "apk add curl; curl -v -H 'X-Scope-OrgID: acme-42' https://prom-remote-write.redwood-inference/api/v1/receive/status"`

maya: Customer ran that and they see `TLS handshake failure` in the curl output. Could be SNI mismatch — we rotated certs last week. We require SNI `prom-remote-write.redwood-inference`.

sam: Filed INC-987 with the details and attached a small script to replicate the curl from within a pod. Also opened PR #458 that attempts an SNI fallback in the proxy. devon — can you take a quick look at the PR?

devon: :thumbsup: I will review. In the meantime, for a quick functional test you can send a one-off remote-write body (compressed protobuf) to the endpoint to validate it accepts data. Example test curl (replace sample.pb):
```sh
curl -v -H "X-Scope-OrgID: acme-42" -H "Content-Type: application/x-protobuf" \
  --data-binary @sample.pb \
  https://prom-remote-write.redwood-inference/api/v1/receive
```

priya: If logs show 401/403 then check token rotation: customers using sigv4/proxy auth need secret `prom-remote-write.token` updated. For TLS issues, confirm their egress NAT is not terminating TLS and that SNI is preserved. Our docs: https://docs.redwood.com/priv-vpc/obs/prom-remote-write (includes promtail example).

observability-bot: [alert] NoSeriesHigh for dashboard acme/overview triggered at 2025-06-12T10:03:00Z -> routed to #support-acme

maya: Thanks — I've asked the customer to paste promtail logs and the curl output into INC-987. Sam, ping me when PR #458 is reviewed so I can coordinate a canary deploy.

sam: Will do. Also posting a direct Explore link for convenience (replace orgId as needed):
https://grafana.redwood-inference/d/acme-42/explore?orgId=acme-42&var-query=sum(rate(app_requests[5m]))

devon: One more troubleshooting tip: if you see `no series` but our proxy logs show `200 OK`, check retention windows and label rewriting rules — sometimes `job`/`instance` label masking causes queries to no-match. Use `label_values(app_requests, job)` in Explore to confirm labels are present.

maya: Added the customer's logs to INC-987 and flagged the TLS handshake output. I'll update here when they re-run the debug pod. Thanks all for the rapid help!"
